component: Installed module identity and local RECORD association
constraints: Inspect actual import locations in an isolated Python process; compare eight selected source files to a trusted checkout and local distribution membership/hash/size.
Static name/version must each have exactly one matching header; local metadata is not publisher authentication or loaded-bytecode attestation.
alternatives: Python importlib.metadata directly reports the distribution used by the target interpreter. Java/Kotlin or Node subprocess orchestration still requires a Python probe for this identity.
Hatchling and Maturin are credible packaging alternatives, but changing the build backend does not prove the executing import identity or publisher authenticity.
rationale: KEEP the direct Python checker: seventeen real-file negative/positive methods pass for source-tree imports, byte changes, RECORD membership/location/digest/size and identity header cardinality.
No runtime or contract mismatch demonstrated. The strict regular-wheel profile deliberately requires RECORD hashes and sizes even where general metadata permits omission.
limits: Official-source candidate comparison only; no alternative executable or speed benchmark.
Local focused source tests only; no new installed distribution, hosted matrix, P19 customer acceptance, physical, hard-real-time, MLS/CNSA or availability claim.
